title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 7: Augustine — if an elect perished God would be deceived and overcome
pass_a_gloss: And hence Augustine infers that if any of the elect departed from God by the mutability of his free will, God would not only be deceived but overcome — because he not only foresaw that the elect would be glorified, but decreed to effect this by an invincible chain of causes. Of these (that is, the elect), if anyone perishes, God is deceived; but none of them perishes, because God is not deceived: of these, if anyone perishes by human fault, God is overcome; but none of them perishes, because God is overcome by nothing (On Rebuke and Grace, ch. 7). Why would God be overcome if an elect perished by the fault of his own will? Because God took it on himself to generate in all the elect not a bare and languid possibility, but a firm, certain, and invincible will to persevere.
pass_b_english: That is why Augustine says: if any elect left God by free will's changeableness, God would not only be deceived but beaten — he not only foresaw their glorification; he decreed to bring it about by an unbeatable chain of causes. On Rebuke and Grace 7: if any of them perishes, God is deceived — but none does, for God is not deceived; if any perishes by human fault, God is overcome — but none does, for nothing overcomes God. Why "overcome" if an elect fell by his own will's fault? Because God undertook to plant in every elect not a thin bare possibility, but a firm, sure, unconquered will to persevere.
source_text: Atque hinc est quod Augustinus infert, si aliquis electorum a Deo discederet mutabilitate liberi sui arbitrii, quod non modo falleretur Deus, sed vinceretur, quia scilicet non modo praevidit electos fore glorificandos, sed invicta causarum concatenatione hoc efficere decrevit. Horum (id est, electorum) si quisquam perit, fallitur Deus; sed nemo eorum perit, quia non fallitur Deus: horum si quisquam perit vitio humano, vincitur Deus; sed nemo eorum perit, quia nulla re vincitur Deus, De corrept. & grat. cap. 7. Cur Deus vinceretur si electus periret vitio propriae voluntatis? Quia scilicet in se Deus suscepit, ut omnibus electis non nudam & languidam possibilitatem, sed firmam, certam & invictam perseverandi voluntatem ingeneraret.
